# Fireworks raises every on-demand GPU rate from September 1, 2026

Existing customers got about three weeks’ notice: the pricing page lists both rates side by side, one column “upto Aug 31” and one “from Sep 1”. Until this update every GPU on the card had a single hourly rate.

What it means for buyers. Blackwell capacity takes the biggest hit: B200 rises 30% and B300 25%, against 14% for H100/H200 and 11% for GB300. If you run dedicated deployments, re-check per-token break-even against Fireworks’ serverless rates. Region-restricted deployments are priced at 1.5x these rates, so they rise by the same percentages.

highlights:
Zettabyte Launches Model-as-a-Service on zCLOUD

# Zettabyte Launches Model-as-a-Service on zCLOUD

August 12, 2026 · Joyce Y.

- Provides access to NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs;

- Offers three fully managed ways to access capacity, backed by a 99.5 percent uptime SLA target;

TAIPEI CITY, Taiwan -- Zettabyte, a global AI computing company, today announced the general availability of Model-as-a-Service on zCLOUD, its GPU cloud. Teams can efficiently call open-source models through API on Zettabyte's NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs.

Model-as-a-Service

With Model-as-a-Service, zCLOUD hosts popular open weight and open-source models, ready to call through an API and run on Zettabyte's GPUs. Teams can build on them directly, without sourcing, installing, and tuning a model themselves. Teams that want raw capacity can still rent GPUs on zCLOUD and run their own models.

GPU Availability

NVIDIA H100 is available today, with pricing from US$1.99 per GPU-hour depending on needs and scale. zCLOUD is backed by a 99.5 percent uptime SLA target, and reserved clusters are built to deploy in under six hours from confirmed requirements.

Ways to Access GPU Capacity

Zettabyte offers three ways to access capacity:

- Short-Term Capacity - GPU instances that scale to hundreds of GPUs, with no long-term commitment.

- Reserved Clusters - Predictable, fully managed capacity for sustained training and inference under a term commitment.

- Private Cloud - Custom deployments for teams with procurement, security, or region requirements.

results.title: GPU Infrastructure Management for ML Teams | AI.info
highlights:
Pretraining and large distributed training are bandwidth- and interconnect-bound. You're moving activations and gradients across hundreds of GPUs, so NVLink domain size and HBM bandwidth matter more than raw FLOPs. That is where NVIDIA's SXM-form-factor parts belong: H100 SXM5 (80GB HBM3, ~3.35 TB/s bandwidth), H200 (141GB HBM3e, ~4.8 TB/s — 76% more memory and 43% more bandwidth than H100), and Blackwell-generation B200 (192GB HBM3e, ~8 TB/s, roughly 2.3x the compute and 1.7x the bandwidth of H200).

At the rack level, GB200 NVL72 pairs Grace CPUs with Blackwell GPUs into a 72-GPU NVLink domain, and GB300 (Blackwell Ultra) uses the same fabric with more memory per GPU. NVIDIA quotes a GB300 NVL72 rack at 20TB of GPU memory and up to 576 TB/s of bandwidth across its 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs. Both are line items on public price sheets now rather than roadmap entries — CoreWeave lists GB200 NVL72, GB300 NVL72 and HGX B300 alongside H100 and A100.

...

| --- | --- | --- |

| H200 | 141GB HBM3e | ~4.8 TB/s |
| B200 | 192GB HBM3e | ~8 TB/s |

## Spot vs. Reserved vs. On-Demand

Cloud GPU capacity comes in three flavors with materially different pricing and risk profiles, and planning should map workload tolerance to capacity type deliberately.

- On-demand is your ceiling price and safety net — AWS P5 (H100) on-demand runs around $6.88/GPU-hour ($55.04/hour for a p5.48xlarge with 8 H100s). Use it for anything you can't afford to have interrupted mid-run.
- Reserved / Capacity Blocks (AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, similar constructs elsewhere) require advance purchase for a fixed duration and guarantee availability without interruption — useful for a planned pretraining run where you know start date and duration but want price certainty.
- Spot cuts cost by roughly 60–70% versus on-demand on AWS P5, but comes with interruption risk that varies significantly by GPU type — H100 spot interruption rates on AWS run under 5%, while A100 spot interruption is meaningfully higher at 15–20%, reflecting differing supply/demand balance.

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Spot savings vs on-demand (AWS P5) | ~60-70% cheaper |
| H100 spot interruption rate | under 5% |
| A100 spot interruption rate | 15-20% |

Neocloud providers add a fourth axis worth comparing against hyperscaler pricing. CoreWeave's North America list price for an 8-GPU HGX H100 node is $49.24 per hour — about $6.16 per GPU-hour — with HGX H200 at $50.44 per node and an 8-GPU A100 node at $21.60, roughly $2.70 per GPU-hour. The Blackwell tiers are quoted the same way: HGX B200 at $68.80 per node, about $8.60 per GPU-hour, a 4-GPU GB200 NVL72 instance at $42.00, and GB300 NVL72 and HGX B300 on request. Neocloud rates often sit meaningfully below hyperscaler on-demand for the same silicon, at the cost of a less mature managed-service ecosystem.

results.title: CME Group Sets 5 October Launch for Compute Futures as GPU Rental Costs Become a Hedgeable Risk
highlights:
CME Group and GPU market intelligence and benchmarking firm Silicon Data have announced plans to launch two Compute futures contracts on 5 October 2026, subject to regulatory review. The contracts will give AI developers, cloud operators and investors a regulated way to hedge the cost of processing power, an input that has moved from a line item in a technology budget to one of the largest variable costs in the global economy.

Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures and Silicon Data B200 Rental Index Futures will track indices measuring hourly GPU rental costs published by Silicon Data, which is backed by global trading firm DRW. Each contract represents a month's worth of rent for the Nvidia H100, the chip at the centre of the current AI build out, and the next generation Nvidia Blackwell B200 respectively. The contracts are cash settled against the indices rather than involving any physical delivery of hardware, and will be listed under the rules of NYMEX.

...

Renting AI compute has until now been a matter of private negotiation, with prices varying widely by provider, contract length and demand conditions.

results.title: Hyperscaler vs Neocloud vs GPU Marketplace · GPUVerse Blog
highlights:
The GPU cloud market has stratified into three distinct tiers: hyperscalers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle Cloud) selling compliance and ecosystem at a premium; neoclouds (CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Crusoe, RunPod) selling specialized GPU infrastructure near cost; and marketplaces (Vast.ai) selling raw capacity at the market floor. The same H100 spans a 2–3x price range across these tiers as of August 2026, because the three tiers are not selling the same product. This article maps what each one actually sells, using the 10 providers in the GPUVerse catalog.

...

The premium is substantial, H100 on-demand commonly runs $4–7/hr against a $1.99/hr market floor, though OCI consistently undercuts its hyperscaler peers, and Google Cloud is unique in offering first-party TPUs (v4, v5e, v6e), a genuinely different accelerator economics covered in our pricing index. All four offer spot capacity at roughly 50–70 percent discounts.

### Neoclouds: specialized GPU infrastructure near cost

The neocloud generation, CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Crusoe, RunPod, builds clouds for AI rather than clouds that also rent GPUs. Their differentiation is focus:

- CoreWeave: Kubernetes-native provisioning, InfiniBand fabric, and the latest NVIDIA hardware first, Blackwell-class fleets at scale for serious training. SOC 2 and ISO 27001, now a large publicly listed operator.
- Lambda: transparent flat pricing and one-click clusters, beloved by researchers; capacity sells out often.
- Nebius: EU-headquartered (Amsterdam) with EU data residency and InfiniBand clusters, the compliance-conscious European choice outside the hyperscalers.
- Crusoe: clean- and stranded-energy powered capacity with reserved clusters, the sustainability story with competitive Hopper pricing.
- RunPod: per-second billing, serverless endpoints, and a community tier alongside vetted Secure Cloud, the fastest path from idea to running GPU.

Pricing sits near the market floor with far stronger reliability than the marketplace tier. The trade-offs: thinner compliance portfolios (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 at best, none offer HIPAA or FedRAMP as of August 2026), fewer regions, fewer managed services. Notably, four of the five (all but RunPod) offer no spot tier, their model is reserved and on-demand capacity, so spot-dependent architectures need to look elsewhere.

...

## The three tiers at a glance

| | Hyperscalers | Neoclouds | Marketplace |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Providers | AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, OCI | CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Crusoe, RunPod | Vast.ai |
| H100-class pricing (Aug 2026) | $4–7/hr on-demand | roughly $2–4/hr | from $1.99/hr |
| Compliance | SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI-DSS (+ FedRAMP on 3) | SOC 2 and/or ISO 27001 | none |
| Reliability | 99%-class, SLA-backed | strong (90–95-class) | host-dependent |
| Spot / interruptible | all four (~50–70% off) | RunPod only (~50% off) | yes (~60% off, bidding) |
| Cluster networking | EFA / InfiniBand / RDMA | InfiniBand on training-focused neoclouds | not guaranteed |
| Best at | regulated and integrated workloads | dedicated AI infrastructure per dollar | absolute lowest cost |

...

### Are neoclouds cheaper than AWS for GPUs?

Substantially, for the GPU itself: H100-class capacity runs roughly $2–4/hr on neoclouds against $4–7/hr hyperscaler on-demand as of August 2026. The gap narrows once egress, integration work, and spot discounts enter the comparison, which is why the honest answer is per-workload arithmetic, not a blanket yes.

highlights: 【AI算力正被包装成一种可融资资产】报道，Silicon Data数据显示，非Hyperscaler市场A100、H100、H200、B200租金分别约1.65、2.72、3.29、5.61美元/GPU小时，H100自去年底2美元明显反弹，B200、H200同步走强。其基于36个月远期租金曲线估算H100残值从去年10月1.4万美元升至目前约2万美元（残值为模型估值，非实际成交价）。 租金走势印证黄仁勋的算力资产化逻辑：GPU稳定产生推理租金后，可像飞机、船舶一样以未来现金流抵押融资。英伟达8月10日联合Apollo、BlackRock等推动超5000亿美元AI基础设施融资，部分贷款以设备抵押，英伟达或按残值提供最高25%担保，该模式若成立将降低Neo-cloud融资成本并反哺GPU需求。 但需注意：Silicon Data自身二手市场数据显示，3年左右的H100挂牌价仅峰值新品的20%—30%，技术折旧仍显著；A100六年租金稳定仅说明老款在推理、微调等低成本场景仍有价值。更准确判断是GPU经济寿命可能长于市场此前假设的2—3年，强劲推理需求正在抵消部分技术折旧，这对5000亿美元融资计划的抵押品估值至关重要。(金十)
